citizens. The printed application form K-35A is used for new and renewal
applications and can be collected from the Department or downloaded from the
website.

Processing fees:

- Normal service: LKR 10,000.00
- Urgent (one-day) service: LKR 20,000.00

The one-day service is only available at the Head Office in Battaramulla.
Applications for the one-day service are accepted between 7.00 a.m. and

prescribed specifications.

english_section:
The eRL service is the official online portal for vehicle revenue licence
renewal in Sri Lanka. The supported vehicle categories include Motor Cars,
Motor Cycles, Dual Purpose Vehicles, Land Vehicles, Three Wheelers, and other
classes maintained by the Department of Motor Traffic.

How the service works:

- First-time users sign up on web.erl2.gov.lk before logging in.
- The user enters the vehicle number and the last 6 digits of the chassis
  number to confirm ownership.
- A valid Insurance Certificate is required. A Vehicle Emission Test
  Certificate is required for vehicle categories where it applies.
- The system accepts credit and debit card payments only.

After payment confirmation, a temporary printable licence valid for 14 days
is sent by email. The official validated licence is then posted to the
registered owner's address by registered post within 7 days.

In-person renewal is available at any convenient Divisional Secretariat
office.

english_section:
Recommended medication for fever and pain: use Paracetamol only, at the dose
prescribed by your doctor. Do NOT use Non-Steroidal Anti-Inflammatory Drugs
(NSAIDs) such as Ibuprofen, Aspirin, Diclofenac Sodium, Mefenamic Acid, or
Celecoxib (tablets or syrup) to reduce fever, because these drugs increase
the risk of bleeding.

Seek immediate medical attention if any warning signs appear:

- persistent vomiting,
- severe abdominal pain,
- bleeding from the gums, nose, or in stools,
- restlessness, lethargy, or cold extremities,
- a sudden drop in temperature accompanied by sweating.

Prevention focuses on eliminating Aedes mosquito breeding sites: empty and
scrub water-holding containers at least once a week, cover all stored water,
and dispose of discarded tyres, tins, and plastic items that collect
rainwater.

Home remedies (papaya leaf juice, lime juice, herbal preparations) are not
proven cures for dengue and must not replace medical care.

english_section:
Influenza is a viral infection. Antibiotics do not treat influenza. Misuse of
antibiotics for viral illnesses contributes to antimicrobial resistance, a
public-health concern that the Ministry of Health has highlighted in
successive advisories.

General precautions during flu season:

- Stay home if you have flu-like symptoms (fever, cough, sore throat).
- Cover coughs and sneezes with a tissue or the elbow.
- Wash hands with soap and water for at least 20 seconds, especially after
  coughing, sneezing, or touching shared surfaces.
- People in high-risk groups (children under 5, adults over 65, pregnant
  women, and people with chronic respiratory or metabolic conditions) should
  consider the seasonal influenza vaccine, which is available privately.

Seek medical attention if symptoms last longer than 7 days, if breathing
becomes difficult, or if a high fever persists beyond 3 days.

english_section:
The Expanded Programme on Immunization (EPI) was launched in Sri Lanka in
1978. The Hib-containing pentavalent vaccine was introduced in 2008. The
programme is delivered free of charge through Medical Officer of Health
(MOH) clinics across the country.

Key milestones from the national immunization schedule:

- BCG vaccine: administered at 0 to 4 weeks of age, before the newborn
  leaves the hospital, often within 24 hours of birth.
- Pentavalent (DTP-HepB-Hib) vaccine: administered in the infancy series.
- MMR vaccine: a national MMR Catch-up Immunization Programme was launched
  on 6 January 2024 by the Epidemiology Unit, targeting children aged
  9 months to 15 years who missed their routine MMR doses.

A child should not be vaccinated when they have a fever above 38 degrees
Celsius on the day of the appointment. The vaccination should be rescheduled
with the MOH clinic. Mild low-grade fever and soreness at the injection site
within 24 to 48 hours are normal post-vaccination reactions.

english_section:
The Department of Meteorology issues cyclone warnings and severe-weather
advisories for Sri Lanka. During cyclone preparedness in coastal districts,
households are advised to:

- Secure loose objects around the home and identify the nearest safe
  building or evacuation shelter.
- Store at least three days of drinking water per family member, and
  charge mobile phones and power banks once a warning is issued.
- Keep important documents in a waterproof container, and pack a small
  emergency kit (medication, identification copies, torch, first-aid).

During the cyclone passage:

- Stay indoors. Move to an interior room away from windows.
- The eye of the cyclone passing overhead can create a deceptive calm of
  about 20 to 30 minutes before high winds resume from the opposite
  direction. Do not go outside during this calm.

After the cyclone has passed, watch for downed power lines, broken glass,
and structurally damaged buildings. Downed lines should be reported to the
Ceylon Electricity Board.

english_section:
The Disaster Management Centre (DMC) has been allocated 117 as its
emergency telephone number. A dedicated telephone line was established for
the public to communicate with the DMC. The Call Centre is operating
24 hours a day, 7 days a week with 21 call operators.

During floods and other declared disasters, the DMC issues Situation
Reports through its public-facing reports portal. Citizens are advised to
check the DMC site for the current bulletin before relying on older
publications.

General flood safety advice issued by DMC and partner agencies:

- Do not wade through flowing water deeper than ankle depth on foot.
- Vehicles should not be driven through flooded roads; even six inches of
  fast-flowing water can sweep a car off the road.
- After flood waters recede, drinking water from open wells should be
  boiled for at least one minute or treated with chlorine tablets, because
  standing flood water often contains sewage and chemical runoff.

english_section:
The National Building Research Organisation (NBRO) issues landslide early
warnings based on 24-hour rainfall thresholds.

- Yellow (Level 1) warning: when rainfall in the previous 24 hours exceeds
  75 mm, the public should be aware of the possibility of landslides,
  slope failures, rock falls, cut-slope failure, and ground subsidence,
  and should be prepared to evacuate to a safe location if necessary.

Special attention should be paid to all hilly areas, to man-made cut-slope
roads within the affected districts, and in particular to all landslide-prone
sites previously designated by NBRO.

Early warning signs that require immediate action include:

- new cracks in walls, floors, or the ground,
- doors or windows that suddenly start sticking,
- tilted trees or fences,
- water seeping from unusual locations on a slope.

If severe landslide signs are observed, the public should promptly inform
the relevant authorities and evacuate to a safer place to avoid the risks.
